cards.lore: The first thing in any system that matters. Everything awful that follows begins with their report.
cards.power: Play to view opponent's hand. If caught, discard your entire deck.

cards.lore: Piloted by a "young" Vael—which means it's only been alive for a few centuries.
cards.power: Bypass all electronic traps. The ship literally out-vibes the radar.

cards.lore: Ossian scouts interpret "survey the system" as "establish the Hegemony's claim by shooting the scenery."
cards.power: Deal 2 damage to a neutral target just to establish dominance.

cards.lore: The galaxy's nervous system, crewed by fatalists hauling diplomatic secrets worth more than their lives.
cards.power: Move an objective instantly. The ship takes 1 damage per transit until it vaporizes.

cards.lore: The circulatory system of a dying galaxy. If they stop arriving, the sector is already dead.
cards.power: Generate 3 Resource tokens. Extrapolate opponent's strategy based on their discards.

cards.lore: Where junior officers learn to juggle combat, politics, and broken engines before they inevitably get court-martialed.
cards.power: Block one attack against a Hauler. Farm mid-level management stress.

cards.lore: Pure, unadulterated aggression shoved into an undersized hull.
cards.power: Double attack power, half defense. Cannot retreat. Ever.

cards.lore: Why fire a torpedo when you can just delete the enemy's bank account from orbit?
cards.power: Cancel opponent's attack by burying them in legal injunctions and electronic warfare.

cards.lore: A floating geopolitical argument. Too expensive to lose, too massive to hide.
cards.power: Instantly claim a system. Opponent must spend 5 turns complaining to the galactic UN.

cards.lore: A ship with a kill-count so high it constitutes a distinct gravitational anomaly.
cards.power: Eradicate target system. Costs the industrial output of your entire hand.

cards.lore: A sovereign community in transit. The ultimate geopolitical headache for every border guard.
cards.power: Relocate your home base. Becomes politically immune to standard attacks.

cards.lore: Officially, it doesn't exist. Unofficially, it just overthrew your planetary government.
cards.power: Execute an action completely off the record. If accused, deny everything.

cards.lore: A paradise that everyone wants, resulting in an eternal, bloody stalemate. Only 1,200 exist; 49 caused wars.
cards.power: Generate infinite diplomatic disputes. Draw 2 conflict cards per turn.

cards.lore: Where civilizations dump their working class to breathe heavy metals and build empires.
cards.power: Triple production speed, but discard 1 population card every turn.

cards.lore: The galaxy's archaeological record. What killed them is probably still down there waiting for you.
cards.power: Draw a high-level Tech card. Flip a coin; on tails, your active crew dies horribly.

cards.lore: A Mycel biological weapon disguised as agriculture. Unstoppable, inevitable ecology.
cards.power: Terraforms target zone. No non-Mycel cards can be played here ever again.

cards.lore: A cosmopolitan cesspool where bartenders have better geopolitical intel than four-star admirals.
cards.power: Swap hands with an opponent in the neutral zone. Ignore all faction laws.

cards.lore: The world that breaks the physics engine. Careers end here; legends begin here.
cards.power: Roll a die. Whatever happens, the Dreshkai Insurance actuaries won't cover it.

cards.lore: A legal dispute maintained for 12,000 years. Peace through mutual bureaucratic exhaustion.
cards.power: Freeze target planet. No one can use it until a treaty is broken.

cards.lore: 8,400 years ago, the working class struck fear into warlords. The only good thing the Hegemony ever did.
cards.power: Instigate a labor strike on opponent's Forge World. Production halts.

cards.lore: Making civilizational choices with zero precedent. 17 successes, 9 wars, 2 dead crews. High risk of getting eaten.
cards.power: Introduce a new rule to the game. Neither player understands how it works yet.

cards.lore: The fine line between "legitimate recovery" and "state-sponsored piracy."
cards.power: Steal an artifact from opponent's discard pile. Claim it was yours all along.

cards.lore: Years in isolation treating phenomena as data points. They make terrible dinner guests.
cards.power: Skip two turns. Return with a massive hand advantage and severe social anxiety.

cards.lore: Changing the course of history while leaving zero receipts. 60% of all politics is just this.
cards.power: Sabotage an opponent's play, completely off the record.

cards.lore: Because access is a right that force can deny, but cannot legitimate denying.
cards.power: Force a delivery through an opponent's defense. Survive on sheer luck.

cards.lore: The charts end here. The win condition is simply coming back alive.
cards.power: Draw blindly from the deck. You might win the game, you might instantly die.

cards.lore: Their final transmissions are the only data we have. We wish we didn't have them.
cards.power: Place an anomaly. Any opponent who lands here loses a turn to sheer dread.

cards.lore: The intel the six powers collectively agreed to be terrifying to exploit. Achieved exactly once in 12,000 years.
cards.power: Lock down a piece of information. All six players must agree to reveal it (they won't).

cards.lore: Eight exist. One is natural. Seven show signs of engineering. The Vael refuse to elaborate.
cards.power: Teleport across the board instantly. No fuel cost.

cards.lore: Its transit window is a matter of timing; its destination is a matter of prayer.
cards.power: Portal opens randomly. Transit is pure gambling.

cards.lore: The wound left behind by a cosmic explosion—or something far worse that didn't make the history books.
cards.power: Drive architectures interact with this unpredictably. Reroll all dice.

cards.lore: A 40,000-year-old structured broadcast. It's not a song. It's navigational infrastructure. But for who?
cards.power: Hypnotize opponent's navigation.

cards.lore: It is not empty. The things inside know you are there. It is larger on the inside.
cards.power: Reduce visibility. Opponent plays next card blind.

cards.lore: A gravitational oscillation from something impossibly huge. The Vael have been measuring it for 30,000 years.
cards.power: A pulsing 11,000-year timer. When it triggers, reset the board.

cards.lore: They don't deviate for obstacles. Obstacles deviate for them.
cards.power: Unstoppable force. Ignore all obstacles and defenses in this column.

cards.lore: You remember things that didn't happen to you. The Mycel know why, and they are terrified.
cards.power: Force an opponent to play using your strategy from three turns ago.

cards.lore: Twelve thousand years old. The standard cheat code for an agonizingly vast universe.
cards.power: Move fast, burn stellarite. Leave a highly detectable energy wake.

cards.lore: The Dreshkai's second-largest revenue stream. Physics monetized to the maximum.
cards.power: Instant communication. Bypass Courier transit times.

cards.lore: Merging flesh and metal until neither substrate remembers what it used to be.
cards.power: Upgrade one unit. Statistically likely to either become a god or explode.

cards.lore: The ultimate biological cheat code: turning your mind into software.
cards.power: Transfer consciousness. Survive physical destruction.

cards.lore: Replicating the Prior's tech will instantly break the galactic balance of power. Everyone is trying; everyone is terrified.
cards.power: Risk total annihilation for a +10 advantage.

cards.lore: The most philosophically contested tech. Did you arrive, or just a copy of you?
cards.power: Swap control of two units. Warning: Identity integrity cannot be verified.

cards.lore: The Ossian Hegemony has a classified weapons program for this. Try not to think about it.
cards.power: Alter the lifecycle of a star. Use it as a weapon or a battery.

cards.lore: The oldest nodes are digging up memories that predate all current civilizations.
cards.power: Recover information stored in the physical structure of the galaxy.

cards.lore: Commerce is a weapon. They own the networks, they set the rates, they own you.
cards.power: Monopolize trade routes. Win via compound interest and insurance fraud.

cards.lore: Militarily directed, hierarchically organized, spectacularly productive in the art of killing.
cards.power: Absolute military dominance. Every negotiation is a hostage situation.

cards.lore: They don't need Capital Ships. They are the Capital Ships. They know what's coming.
cards.power: Ignore the rules of the game entirely because you know a secret.

cards.lore: The ultimate archivists. They pay premium rates for uncertainty reduction.
cards.power: Harvest data from every action played. Hoard the galaxy's secrets.

cards.lore: Access is a right. Dispersed, decentralized, and utterly impossible to govern.
cards.power: Improvise. Adapt. Field-expedient modifications that bypass regulations.

cards.lore: Their terraforming is irreversible. They are the galaxy's memory, running on spores.
cards.power: Spread network presence. Overtake enemy bases passively.

cards.lore: They modified the galactic core, left behind stable wormholes, and vanished. Or did they?
cards.power: Leave behind artifacts that drive current civilizations insane.

cards.lore: The face the network shows you while it eats the soil beneath your feet.
cards.power: Engage in diplomacy while the network secretly devours the planet underground.

cards.lore: They aren't just observing the Resonance. They are designed to interact with it.
cards.power: Harness the 11,000-year frequency. End the current era.

cards.lore: The oldest observatory in the galaxy. What exactly was it built to watch for?
cards.power: Look into the deep past. See what's coming.

cards.lore: The Vael's unshared archive. The Sorn couldn't steal it; the Dreshkai couldn't buy it.
cards.power: Uncover the galaxy's final secret. Game over.

cards.lore: "We are not the first ones here, and we are not the last ones coming."
cards.power: The Vael haven't updated this file in 30,000 years because the answer hasn't changed.
